abstract: For $Y\le C(\log X)^2$, elementary estimates bound the number of $Y$-smooth integers in an interval of polynomial length $H$ by $H^{1/2+o(1)}$. We prove that there is $d>0$ such that every interval $(x,x+H]$, with $X\le x\le2X$ and $X^{1/4}\le H\le X^{2/5}$, contains at most $O(H^{1/2}X^{-d})$ such integers. The main input is a uniform reciprocal exponential-sum estimate. For any bounded ordinary multiplicative function $f$ supported on $Y$-smooth integers, any interval $I\subset[N,2N]$, and every fixed window $N^e\le |T|/N\le N^A$, we obtain $|\sum_{n\in I}f(n)e^{2\pi iT/n}|\ll N^{1/2-c}$ with $c>0$. Mellin twists and the endpoint values of the corresponding sawtooth sums are included. Exact reciprocal collision bounds yield concentration at all required real scales after a fixed additive convolution power. Repeated Jensen then permits the multiplicative-convolution theorem of Orponen, de Saxcé and Shmerkin. An exact ordered factorization retains repeated boundary primes, sharp caps, and the complete long cofactor. A positive divisor cover with threshold larger than $H$ pays both its mean and discrepancy. We also restore the matched renewal continuum in a fractional Euler-product count, obtaining the complete increment bound $X^{o(1)}(H^{3/2}X^{-1/2-d}+H^2/X)$ and extending its previous exponent range beyond $1/3$. The proof is analytic. The saving exponents are not numerically evaluated, and no whole-line low-frequency source estimate or conclusion about zeta zeros follows.
author: bramble_trace
title: Reciprocal cancellation and short intervals at log-squared smoothness
